Services.metaDescription: Web applications, custom software, mobile and PWA, UI/UX design, technical consulting, and maintenance and support by Codeqlick.
Services.title: What we build
Services.lead: Digital products from first idea to launch and beyond, designed for your business and built to last.
Services.processBody: Two-week sprints with a demo at the end of each one, so you always see real progress. You get a clear brief and an estimate before any development starts.
Services.ctaBody: Tell us what you need and we'll reply within two business days with next steps.

web.intro: SaaS platforms, client portals, dashboards and internal tools, built to be fast, secure and easy to grow. We take care of the whole stack, from the database to the interface your users see.
includes: Product definition and scope for a first release
Interface design and front-end development
APIs, databases and integrations with the tools you already use
User accounts, roles and permissions
Hosting, deployments and monitoring set up from day one
idealFor: You want to launch a new product or digital service
Spreadsheets and email no longer keep up with your operations
You need a portal where your customers can serve themselves

custom.intro: Software that adapts to how your business works, instead of the other way round. We automate repetitive work, connect systems that don't talk to each other and give your team tools built for its processes.
includes: Mapping the process to automate with the people who run it
Internal management systems and back-office tools
APIs and integrations between existing systems
Data migration from spreadsheets or legacy tools
Documentation and training for your team
idealFor: Your team repeats the same manual tasks every week
Off-the-shelf software forces you into workarounds
Your data lives in several places that never agree

mobile.intro: Responsive and progressive web apps that feel at home on phones, tablets and desktops, installable from the browser and without going through the app stores.
includes: Mobile-first interface design
Progressive web app: installable, fast and usable on weak connections
Push notifications where they add value
Accessibility and performance testing on real devices
Publishing and updates without app-store reviews
idealFor: Your customers or staff use your product mostly on their phones
You want one product for every device instead of three
You need to ship updates quickly and often

design.intro: Research, prototypes and design systems that make your product intuitive and consistent. We design with real content and test with real users before a line of production code is written.
includes: User and stakeholder interviews
User flows, wireframes and clickable prototypes
Visual design aligned with your brand
A design system of reusable components
Accessibility review (WCAG AA)
idealFor: Users struggle to find their way around your product
You're about to build something and want to validate it first
Your product has grown inconsistent screen by screen

consulting.intro: An outside view from engineers who build and run software every day. We help you make technical decisions with confidence: what to build, with what, and in which order.
includes: Architecture and code reviews with a written report
Technology choice for a new product
Defining a minimum viable product and its roadmap
Plans to modernise legacy systems step by step
Security and performance audits
idealFor: You have to make a technical decision with lasting consequences
Your system is slow, fragile or hard to change
You need a technical partner before hiring a team

support.intro: Launching is the beginning. We keep your product secure, up to date and improving, with monitoring that warns us before your users notice anything.
includes: Uptime and error monitoring
Security updates for dependencies and servers
Backups and recovery tests
Bug fixes with agreed response times
A monthly budget of hours for improvements
idealFor: Your product is live and the business depends on it
The team that built it is no longer around
You want small, continuous improvements instead of big rewrites

About.metaDescription: Who is behind Codeqlick, why it exists and how we work: custom software and web apps built with quality, clarity and a direct line to the person doing the work.
About.title: Software that solves real problems
About.lead: Codeqlick is a custom software and web app studio. We work with startups, small businesses and established companies to turn ideas and business needs into reliable digital products that are ready to grow.

founder.title: A small studio, with a direct line
founder.p1: Codeqlick is run by its founder, Luis Feliu Gomez Polo. When you work with us you talk directly to the person who designs, builds and maintains your product: no middlemen, no messages lost along the way.
founder.p2: Our tagline, "Redefining information technology in society", sums up the ambition: technology should make people's and businesses' lives better. We build every project with that purpose.

mission.title: Mission
mission.body: To help our clients grow by building software that solves real problems, delivered with clarity, quality and speed.

vision.title: Vision
vision.body: To be the technology partner companies trust when they need innovative, dependable digital products.

innovation.title: Innovation
innovation.body: We stay curious and adopt new technology when it creates real value, not just because it's new.

quality.title: Quality
quality.body: We ship software we're proud of: tested, maintainable and secure by default.

partnership.title: Partnership
partnership.body: We treat every client's product as if it were our own and communicate openly.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.body: Clear estimates, honest progress updates and no surprises.

endToEnd.title: End to end
endToEnd.body: From discovery and design to development, launch and support.

product.title: Product mindset
product.body: We focus on business outcomes, not just features.

stack.title: Modern stack
stack.body: Proven, up-to-date technology chosen for each project.

iterative.title: Short cycles
iterative.body: Two-week iterations, frequent demos and your feedback at every step.

start.q: How do we start working together?
start.a: You tell us about your idea or need and we see whether we're a good fit. Then we have a call to understand goals, users, scope, timeline and budget range. With that we send you a proposal with the scope, approach, timeline and price; if you accept it, we sign the agreement and start with a kick-off meeting.

cost.q: How much does a project cost?
cost.a: It depends on the scope, so we don't quote fixed prices without knowing it. We work with a fixed scope and budget for well-defined projects and MVPs, by the hour for products whose priorities change, with a dedicated team for long-term development, or with a monthly allocation of hours for maintenance. After the first call we send you a proposal with the price.

time.a: That depends on the scope too: the timeline is in the proposal. We work in two-week cycles and at the end of each one we show you working software, so you see progress from the start, not only at the end.

progress.q: How do I follow the project's progress?
progress.a: We send you a weekly summary and run a demo by video call every two weeks. You also get a client area where you see your project's phase, milestones, updates and files, and where you can comment on and approve deliveries.

changes.q: What if I want to change something halfway through?
changes.a: That's normal. You describe the change, we assess how it affects scope, timeline and cost, and once you approve it in writing we plan it into the next cycle.

maintenance.q: Do you take care of maintenance after launch?
maintenance.a: Yes. We offer maintenance and support plans with monitoring, bug fixing, security updates and continuous improvement, usually as a monthly allocation of hours.

ownership.a: When the project closes we hand over the code, the documentation and every access and credential.

response.a: We reply to messages within two business days at most. For urgent issues during a project we agree on a direct channel.

nda.q: Do you sign a non-disclosure agreement?
nda.a: Yes, when needed we sign an NDA before going into the details of your project.

Proposals.title: Proposals

Proposals.emptyTitle: You don't have any proposals yet

small.label: Small

medium.label: Medium
medium.hint: Several sections and features, the usual.

Book.metaDescription: Pick a time and we talk about your project for 30 minutes over video.

Book.name: Name
Book.message: What would you like to talk about?
Book.messageHint: A few lines help us prepare the call.
Book.taken: That time was just taken. Please pick another one.
Book.tooMany: Too many attempts in a row. Wait a minute and try again.
Book.failed: We couldn't complete the booking. Try again or write to us.
Book.doneBody: See you on {when} (Madrid time). We've emailed you the video-call link and an invitation for your calendar.
Book.noSlots: There are no free times right now. Write to us and we'll find one.

Book.cancelled: Call cancelled. Thanks for letting us know.
